patch.value: Managed npm update checks report a subprocess timeout as npm_registry_lookup_failed, and the fixed 10 s npm view budget makes the Windows nightly extension-freshness test flaky

Nightly run 44087418672 (GitHub alert issue 1747, windows-latest Node 24 shard 4/4) failed tests/integration/extensions/extension-diagnostic-purity.integration.spec.ts in both the initial attempt and the retry (21.6 s for two attempts) at its first registry-backed freshness check: update_check_status was failed instead of checked. The test passes in 5.3 s on green Windows nights (run 43867277935) while spawning npm view several times, so each failing attempt spent the full GITHUB_UPDATE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS (10 s) on one cold npm view through the Windows command shell. runNpmUpdateQuery in src/sdk/extension/update-check.ts maps every failure, including that timeout, to the stable code npm_registry_lookup_failed, so neither the nightly log nor a user's pm extension --manage output can tell a slow npm from an unavailable registry. Proposed: report a distinct stable code for a timed-out lookup (killed subprocess with ETIMEDOUT or SIGTERM) without echoing npm's command, stderr or environment, name the budget in the diagnostic, and give the integration test a deterministic registry check budget so Windows cold npm starts do not fail it. Related evidence work: pm-q7c36n kept subprocess timeout and signal evidence for registry install acceptance; pm-2zjs0g measures nightly family rates.

A timed-out npm update lookup reports a distinct stable code (no npm command, stderr or environment in the output) and the diagnostic names the budget; the extension-diagnostic-purity integration test no longer depends on a cold Windows npm start finishing inside 10 s; unit tests cover the timeout and failure classifications
A slow npm view is reported as a timeout distinct from an unavailable registry, and the Windows nightly freshness test is deterministic
Every lookup failure, including the 10 s timeout, is npm_registry_lookup_failed, and the Windows nightly test failed twice at the timeout

value.text:
Codex review round 1 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh, on f0cbdfc88). The update-check findings and how each was fixed:
- P2: the timeout was inferred from execFile's rejection (killed, and not a maxBuffer overflow). A provider that handles SIGTERM and exits 0 would resolve with partial output. Fix: runBoundedUpdateQuery owns the deadline, a setTimeout that aborts the child through an AbortSignal. A lookup still running when the deadline passes is reported as *_timed_out even when the child then exits cleanly. isExecTimeout and execFile's timeout option are gone. A unit test makes the child exit 0 with partial output on abort.
- P2: the behaviour change had no contract_change declaration. Fix: declared on pm-5kfzjh and pm-43p2c3.
- P3: the summary always carried an update_check_timeout_ms key, as undefined. Fix: the refresh, the normalizer and the summary add the key only when a lookup timed out (withUpdateCheckTimeout, optionalTimeoutBudget). Tests assert the key is absent with not.toHaveProperty.
- P3: the default-budget tests inherited a PM_EXTENSION_UPDATE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS exported by the shell. Fix: they stub it unset and restore it.
- P3: the docs overstated GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. Fix: git also runs with GCM_INTERACTIVE=never, and the docs say that another askpass program or credential helper that prompts can still hold the lookup until its budget runs out.
Abort semantics on Windows: an execFile abort emits an error that destroys the child's stdio and settles at once. It does not wait for a grandchild still holding the pipe, which the timeout option did with shell: true.

value.text: Implemented on branch feat/sdk-stable-consumer-classifications. runNpmUpdateQuery now runs under runBoundedUpdateQuery's explicit deadline. A lookup still running when the budget passes reports npm_registry_lookup_timed_out, and every other failure reports npm_registry_lookup_failed. checkNpmUpdate carries timeout_ms; the managed record and the extension summary carry it as update_check_timeout_ms, present only on a timeout. PM_EXTENSION_UPDATE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS sets the budget for both providers (resolveExtensionUpdateCheckTimeoutMs: integer ms, default 10000, clamped to 1000-120000, and the default for a value that is not finite). The GH-1747 integration test (extension-diagnostic-purity) gives registry-backed checks a 60 s budget, so a cold Windows npm start no longer fails it. It also proves the timeout path end to end: a local registry that answers after 3 s under a 1 s budget reports npm_registry_lookup_timed_out with update_check_timeout_ms 1000. The local run is green in 2.5 s.

value.text:
Codex review round 2 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh, on fd842f55f). The update-check findings and how each was fixed:
- P2: the AbortSignal deadline still waited for the pipes. Node drops the abort listener when the launcher exits, so a descendant holding stdout or stderr kept execFile pending; Codex measured 1.38 s for a 400 ms budget. Aborting also killed only the launcher. Fix: runBoundedUpdateQuery now uses spawn directly, because execFile does not forward detached. The child is spawned detached on POSIX (its own process group) with windowsHide, stdin ignored and stderr drained and discarded, and stdout is bounded by a per-provider maxBuffer (npm 64 KiB, git 1 MiB). The deadline settles the promise on its own, destroys the pipes and calls killProcessTree: SIGKILL to the process group on POSIX, taskkill /T /F on Windows. killProcessTree moved from src/sdk/test/execution.ts into src/core/shared/process-tree.ts so both callers share it. The new tests/integration/extensions/update-check-process-tree.integration.spec.ts (POSIX) runs a fake git that leaves sleep 30 on its pipes and exits 0. The check settles as github_remote_lookup_timed_out in about 1 s, and the descendant is gone within 5 s. On the round-1 design this test would wait the full 30 s.
- P3: a stale stored update_check_timeout_ms survived normalization next to a non-timeout reason. Fix: the managed-state normalizer keeps it only beside npm_registry_lookup_timed_out or github_remote_lookup_timed_out. The codes are spelled locally because importing update-check would close a cycle through install-sources and bundled-catalog. Tests pin both codes and the drop cases.

The Minor about only the direct child being signalled was fixed in the same commit by the process-group or taskkill /T teardown, with a real fake-git integration test.

value.text:
Codex review round 3 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh, on 5af18de6d). Each finding and how it was handled:
- P2: on POSIX the detached lookup group survived Ctrl-C, because it is outside the terminal's foreground process group. Fix: trackDetachedProcessGroup in src/core/shared/process-tree.ts adds listeners only while a lookup is in flight. On exit it kills the tracked groups. On SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP it kills them, removes itself, and re-raises the signal when no other listener remains, so the default exit still applies. A real-process integration test launches the built SDK with a stalled fake git and sends the host SIGINT. The host exits with SIGINT, and the launcher and its descendant are both gone. The negative control (tracking disabled in dist) fails that test.
- P2: when taskkill could not start or failed, nothing was killed. Fix: killProcessTree falls back to killing the root process. runBoundedUpdateQuery also kills a direct child that is still running after the tree teardown, including when the teardown rejects.
- P2: the lock-scope issue again. Now fixed in this PR as pm-9x9drr.
- P2: the 8 s held-registry case brought back the npm start-up dependency. Fix: the purity test's timeout case now runs a stalled npm fixture (sh on POSIX, npm.cmd on Windows) under a 2 s budget, so start-up time no longer decides the outcome.
- P3: an unreaped zombie descendant failed the liveness probe. Fix: the probe treats a process that is gone, or shown by ps with state Z, as stopped.
- P3: the contract_change omitted the keyof ManagedExtensionRecord migration. Fix: before, after and migrate now cover it.

Codex review round 4 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh, on 67c7eef6b). Each finding and how it was handled:
- P2: a host that registered process.once("SIGTERM", shutdown) before a lookup had that listener removed before the cleanup counted listeners. The cleanup saw none and re-raised SIGTERM, cutting the host's async shutdown short. Fix: the cleanup is prepended (prependListener), so it runs first, while the host's once wrapper is still registered, and re-raises only when it is the only listener. A real-process test registers process.once SIGTERM in a host running the built SDK: the host finishes its 200 ms shutdown, writes its marker, exits 0, and the lookup group is gone. The negative control (an appended listener) fails that test.
- P2: freshness mismatch after the lock release, and raw filesystem errors outside the lock's host-error boundary. Both come from the pm-9x9drr lock move, which is reverted out of this PR. pm-9x9drr is open again and records both as design requirements.
- P2: closure and changelog belong in this branch. Done in the same commit: escape class, gate evidence and close evidence on pm-gh1749, pm-5kfzjh and pm-43p2c3, then pnpm changelog:pm.
- P3: the interruption test could leave its host subprocess running if setup failed. Fix: interruptHost kills and awaits the host in a finally block.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 5 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh, on 52d233ceb), and a design change:
- P1: the surface snapshot still recorded the old Decision & ({} | null) default type. Fix: regenerated from main's snapshot. It now records NonNullable<Decision> | Extract<Decision, null> as additive, with the single ManagedExtensionRecord acknowledgement.
- P2 (two findings): a host prependOnceListener added after a lookup starts was still cut off by the re-raise, and a lookup started in a worker thread was detached while its cleanup listeners sat in the worker, which process signals never reach. These are the third and fourth round in which signal handling broke a host. Every listener-ordering rule had another counter-case.
- Decision: stop detaching. Lookups stay in pm's process group, so a terminal Ctrl-C reaches them exactly as before, and pm installs no signal handlers. trackDetachedProcessGroup, its listeners and its unit spec are removed. For a child that is not a group leader, killProcessTree now walks the child's live descendants from one ps snapshot and kills them, then the child. On Windows it is still taskkill /T, with the root-kill fallback. A descendant whose launcher already exited is not reached on either platform, but the deadline already settles the lookup, so it no longer delays the result. The docs say exactly this.
- Tests (POSIX, real processes): a launcher that exits while sleep holds its pipes settles in about 1 s. A still-running launcher and its descendant are both killed at the deadline. A host in its own process group, given SIGINT to the whole group as a terminal Ctrl-C would, exits with SIGINT, and its launcher and foreground helper stop. That fixture uses a foreground helper, because a non-interactive shell's background job ignores SIGINT by POSIX rule.
- The pm-5kfzjh resolution, actual result and gate evidence are corrected to this final design.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex round 6 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh, on e115066c4) and CodeRabbit's second pass (on 52d233ceb). The update-check findings and how each was handled:
- With windowsHide and no inherited stdio, Node starts the provider without a console, so on Windows a Ctrl-C did not reach it. Fix: windowsHide is dropped for the lookup, as the original execFile path never set it.
- The ps snapshot ran synchronously after the timeout and delayed delivering it. Fix: killProcessTree now runs ps through spawn, bounded to 10 s, so the rejection is delivered first and host timers are not blocked.
- PID reuse: a launcher that already exited could be torn down by its recycled PID, and on Windows taskkill took a PID that might have been reused. Fix: stop() tears down by PID only while Node still reports the launcher running. Otherwise it only destroys stdout, and the root is always killed through its ChildProcess handle via killProcessTree's killRoot callback.
- ps -o pid=,ppid= prints only the PID column on FreeBSD. Fix: -o pid= -o ppid=.
- The ps parsing sat inside the c8 ignore block. Fix: descendantsFromProcessTable is a pure, exported function covered by tests/unit/core/shared/process-tree.spec.ts (deepest-first order, absent root, malformed rows, cycles, re-parented helpers).
- CodeRabbit: taskkill was resolved by name, through the working directory or PATH. Fix: the absolute System32 path from SystemRoot. Its run is bounded to 10 s, and the root is killed if it fails or stalls.
- CodeRabbit: a piped stderr held by a descendant delayed close. Fix: stdio is ignore, pipe, ignore.
- CodeRabbit: a git exit code of 128 with a descendant holding stdout waited for the deadline and reported a timeout. Fix: a failed exit settles at once as *_lookup_failed and destroys stdout. A clean exit still waits for close, so the output is complete.
- CodeRabbit: test strictness. The no-timeout summary now asserts the key is absent, the ps probe fails loudly when ps cannot run, and the Ctrl-C test bounds its exit wait inside try so the finally block always reaps the host.
- CodeRabbit: the git prompt wording now says the prompts are suppressed, not that the lookup fails at once.
- Declined: a Windows Job Object, so taskkill could reach a descendant whose launcher already exited. Node exposes no job-object API, and the limitation is documented. The guarantee that matters, a deadline that never waits for such a descendant, holds.
- Obsolete: CodeRabbit's interruption-scope and Windows host-exit comments, because e115066c4 removed the signal handling.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 7 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh, on a8a27f03f). Each finding and how it was fixed:
- P2: when spawn runs out of descriptors (EMFILE), it can return a child without stdout and emit error on the next tick. The runner touched stdout before registering its error listener, so that error could crash the host. Fix: runBoundedUpdateQuery and runTeardownHelper register the error listener first and settle as failed when there is no stdout. A unit test spawns a stdout-less child and then emits EMFILE.
- P2: the teardown helpers could stall without a close event. Fix: runTeardownHelper has its own hard 10 s deadline, after which it resolves without a result, destroys stdout and SIGKILLs the helper. Spawn's timeout option is no longer used.
- P2: PID reuse while the asynchronous ps ran. Fix: killProcessTree takes a ProcessTreeRoot { kill, alive }. The runner passes alive = Node has not reported the child's exit. An unreaped child's PID cannot be reused: libuv reaps it and Node sets exitCode in the same callback, and on Windows the open process handle pins the PID. The snapshot is used only if alive() still holds after ps returns; otherwise no descendant is signalled and the root is killed through its handle.
- process-tree.ts is no longer excluded from coverage. tests/unit/core/shared/process-tree.spec.ts mocks spawn, process.kill and the platform, and covers the parser, the helper (success, spawn throw, error, no stdout, stall), the group signal, the descendant walk, the discarded snapshot, the ps failure, the System32 taskkill path including its SystemRoot fallback, and the root-kill fallback.

patch.value: It reports npm_registry_lookup_timed_out, and the managed record and extension summary carry update_check_timeout_ms naming the budget; other failures still report npm_registry_lookup_failed; PM_EXTENSION_UPDATE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS sets the budget (default 10000, clamped to 1000-25000)

Update lookups run under runBoundedUpdateQuery. It spawns the provider attached to pm's process group and console (stdin and stderr ignored, stdout capped), so a terminal Ctrl-C reaches it with pm and no signal handlers are installed. Its own deadline settles the lookup without waiting for the pipes. It then kills a launcher that is still running and that launcher's live descendants: taskkill /T from System32 on Windows, or the system ps (/bin/ps or /usr/bin/ps) tree walk elsewhere, used only when ps exits cleanly and the root is still unreaped. The root is always killed through its ChildProcess handle. A failed exit settles at once, and a later clean exit cannot replace a timed-out result. A lookup still running at its budget reports npm_registry_lookup_timed_out with update_check_timeout_ms; the summary carries the budget only on a failed check. Other failures report npm_registry_lookup_failed. PM_EXTENSION_UPDATE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS sets the budget (default 10000, clamped to 1000-25000, below the 30-second extension state lock wait). The GH-1747 test gives real npm the 25 s maximum, plus a stalled npm fixture under 2 s.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 8 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh, on df7e6ce04). Each finding and how it was handled:
- P2: ps was resolved through PATH, yet its output decides which processes get SIGKILL. Fix: resolveTrustedPs uses /bin/ps or /usr/bin/ps only. The snapshot is used only when ps exits 0; otherwise only the root is stopped. Unit tests cover ps not installed and ps exiting with an error.
- P2: the lock scope, raised a third time. Mitigation here: PM_EXTENSION_UPDATE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS is clamped to at most 25000 ms, below the extension state lock's 30-second wait (120 attempts of 250 ms), so one lookup run under that lock cannot outlast a concurrent package action. That is the regression the raised budget introduced. Several lookup batches under the lock is pre-existing and is pm-9x9drr's structural fix. The docs, contract_change and resolution say 1000-25000.
- P3, declined with reason: a descendant could exit and have its PID reused in the microseconds between the ps snapshot and the signal. PID-based signalling cannot rule that out, and the only alternatives are OS containment (a Linux pidfd per descendant, a Windows job object) that Node does not expose for descendants. Reuse within that window requires the PID space to wrap around. The killProcessTree doc comment states this limit.
- P3: a stale stored budget on a skipped (local or built-in) record was copied into the summary. Fix: buildInstalledExtensionSummary emits update_check_timeout_ms only when the resolved status is failed. extension-command.spec.ts asserts it is absent for skipped_non_github and present for a failed timeout.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 9 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh, on c86dc7aec). Each finding and how it was handled:
- P2: the 25 s cap bounded each lookup but not the whole scan under the lock. Five slow providers make two batches, about 50 s, against the 30 s lock wait. Fix: refreshManagedExtensionUpdates, checkNpmUpdate and checkGithubUpdate take an explicit timeoutMs, and manage --fix-managed-state passes EXTENSION_UPDATE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS, so the lookups it runs under the lock behave exactly as on main. The override applies everywhere else. The integration test runs --fix-managed-state with the override at 2000 and asserts update_check_timeout_ms 10000. The docs and contract_change say so.
- P2: when the host's event loop was blocked across the deadline, a queued exit or close could run before the overdue timer and be reported as an ordinary result. Fix: the runner records a monotonic deadline with performance.now(), and settle reports *_timed_out for any outcome processed at or after it. A unit test advances performance.now past the budget before the child closes cleanly and expects a timeout.
- P2, declined with reason: on Windows the root could exit and have its PID reused in the moment before taskkill opens it. Only a job object, which Node does not expose, would close that window; the root is checked as unreaped immediately before taskkill starts. The killProcessTree doc comment states the limit.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
CodeRabbit's third full pass (on c86dc7aec): 12 minor findings, all fixed.
- Teardown identity: the Windows taskkill fallback now kills the root only if root.alive() still holds after taskkill fails, so a root that exited during taskkill is not killed by a possibly reused PID. The linked-test runner (src/sdk/test/execution.ts) now passes killProcessTree a root bound to its ChildProcess, as update-check does.
- Tests:
  - The POSIX ps-pending test flips alive() to false inside the fake ps, so checking alive() before ps started would fail it.
  - The update-check teardown test records alive() and asserts it after the lookup.
  - The liveness probe accepts only ps status 1 with no row as gone; anything else throws.
  - The live-tree fixture waits for its single recorded sleep instead of starting a second one.
  - The Ctrl-C host test listens for error, settles on close, bounds its cleanup wait, and records each PID as soon as it is read.
- pm-43p2c3: a real fake git writes a credential-shaped marker to stderr and exits 128. The test asserts github_remote_lookup_failed and that the marker is absent. Its gate evidence cites this test.
- Docs: descendant teardown is described as best effort, and the timeout result never depends on it. pm-9x9drr's description now states the current 25 s cap and the interim mitigation, and has a reproduction comment.
- Runtime entrypoint (declined): ./sdk/runtime has never exported the mutation guard. The PR description, which wrongly claimed it did, is corrected.
- The local full coverage run of the round-9 code had 3 timing failures under coverage and host load: scale-benchmark and deps-command hit the 30 s timeout, and the secret-guard linear-scan bound measured 5228 ms against 5000. All three pass when run on their own. They also passed in the hosted coverage run on e115066c4, so they are not regressions.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 10 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh, on a486e4799). Each finding and how it was fixed:
- P2: stop() destroyed stdout before the ps snapshot, so a provider still writing could take SIGPIPE, exit and orphan its helpers before ps listed them. Fix: at the deadline the runner stops collecting (data after settle is discarded), keeps stdout open while killProcessTree captures and kills the tree, and closes the pipe only afterwards. A unit test holds the teardown open and asserts that stdout stays open and that overflow data cannot start a second teardown.
- P2: refreshManagedExtensionUpdates freed a worker slot as soon as a lookup timed out, while the teardown might still be running, so more than four providers could be alive. Fix: UpdateQueryError carries its teardown promise, failedUpdateStatus records it in a WeakMap (off the serialisable status), and updateCheckTeardown(status) lets the refresh worker hold its slot until the teardown finishes. A direct checkNpmUpdate or checkGithubUpdate still returns at the deadline. A unit test holds the teardown and asserts the refresh does not complete until it is released.
- P3: procps rejects -A under PS_PERSONALITY=bsd or CMD_ENV=bsd. Fix: the ps snapshot runs with a fixed environment, PATH=/usr/bin:/bin and LC_ALL=C. A unit test asserts that environment, and that taskkill keeps the inherited one.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Codex review round 11 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh, on 29a0847a4). Each finding and how it was fixed:
- P2: the round-10 slot retention made pm package manage wait for each batch's teardown, up to 10 s, before returning its results. Under --fix-managed-state that also kept the state lock. Fix: refreshManagedExtensionUpdates separates the two. A counting semaphore (createPermits, limit 4) is acquired before each lookup and released only when updateCheckTeardown(status) settles, so no more than four providers are ever alive. The worker itself returns its entry as soon as the lookup settles, so results, and the lock, never wait for a teardown. Unit test: with five stalled providers the fifth starts only after a teardown releases its permit, and the refresh resolves while four teardowns are still pending.
- P2: an empty or relative SystemRoot made the taskkill path relative. Codex review round 13 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh, on 273da38dd). How each finding was handled:
- P2, declined with reason: a provider stuck in uninterruptible I/O can ignore SIGKILL beyond the 2 s exit wait, and its permit is then released while it is still alive. Never releasing until a real exit would let a permanently stuck provider (or four of them) hang pm package manage, which breaks the documented bounded timeout result. Deferring later lookups would need a new reason code, a contract change for a kernel or storage fault, not a provider behaviour. The current overshoot is bounded: every extra live provider has already been sent SIGKILL, and there are at most as many as there are managed packages.
- P3: test cleanup relied on the command name, so a recycled PID running sleep, sh or git could be killed. Fix: readPids captures each fixture process's start time (ps -o lstart=, with a fixed environment), and killQuietly signals a pid only while its current start time equals the captured one.

Codex review round 16 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh, on 3ec43cf6a). Both findings fixed:
- P2: descendant identity, raised for the fourth time across reviewers. Instead of declining again, the teardown now narrows the window. descendantEntriesFromProcessTable keeps each descendant's snapshot parent. Right before signalling, parentStillMatches re-reads /proc/<pid>/stat on Linux (the ppid is parsed after the command name's last closing parenthesis) and skips a PID whose parent changed. Descendants are killed deepest first, so a live parent's children are checked while that parent is still alive. A PID that vanished is skipped; without procfs (macOS, BSD) the snapshot is trusted, which is documented. killProcessTree is split into killWindowsTree and killPosixDescendants to stay under the complexity ceiling.
- P2: a teardown helper (ps or taskkill) that cannot die after its 2 s deadline is now unref'd, so it cannot keep pm running, matching the provider teardown.
Tests cover command names with spaces and parentheses, reused and vanished PIDs with and without procfs, the default /proc read, a skipped reused descendant in killProcessTree, and the helper unref. The unit spec mocks readFileSync, so a fake PID never reads a real process's /proc entry.

CodeRabbit's sixth pass (on 64341881a): 15 minor findings. 14 fixed, 1 declined.
- Code: at the deadline the timeout is now delivered first. The teardown, whose first steps are synchronous process and filesystem checks (process.kill on the group, existsSync, /proc reads), starts in a zero-delay timer on a later turn of the event loop. Writing the tests for this exposed a real ordering bug: the overdue branch of settle (performance.now() at or past the deadline) built its error from a teardown variable that was not yet set, so the deferred teardown was lost and a provider slot was freed early. The deadline handler now records the deferred teardown before settling. A unit test pins that the result arrives before teardown starts.
- Code: the managed-state normalizer trims update_error before recognising a timeout, as the extension summary does, for both the budget and the availability.
- Records: pm-gh1749's contract says "defined own entry" (an undefined entry falls through). pm-43p2c3's contract and resolution, and pm-5kfzjh's contract, limit the failed codes to execution failures, since output-validation codes such as no_remote_reference_found and invalid_npm_registry_metadata stay separate. pm-9x9drr's actual result no longer counts teardown time under the lock. pm-gh1749's linked type test now runs pnpm build first, because the type tests resolve the package's dist declarations.
- Docs: inheritance holds only without a defined own rules entry; immediate failure only for exits observed before the deadline; the SecretGuardPolicy JSDoc on unshipped rule keys.
- Tests: the offline override provably makes no request; the ps probe is bounded (5 s, SIGKILL); the stderr fixture writes a marker proving it ran; non-timeout results use toStrictEqual.
- Declined: on Windows with both SystemRoot and windir unset, the linked-test runner no longer finds taskkill on PATH. Resolving it through PATH or the working directory is exactly what the trusted-path change removed, and Windows always sets SystemRoot, so only a deliberately stripped SDK host environment loses tree teardown. Its root is still killed.

Codex review of 27f7c3426: two P2 findings, both fixed.
- A host that exits right after a timeout result, such as an SDK host calling process.exit(), could abandon the deferred teardown before any signal was sent, leaving npm or git itself running. Fix: while a teardown is pending, one shared exit listener (no signal handlers) synchronously kills each pending provider through its ChildProcess handle. The listener exists only while a teardown is pending, and a unit test asserts it is added once, kills the provider, and is removed. The pm CLI never calls process.exit, so its teardown always runs in full.
- Earlier releases persisted a failed GitHub check as git's command line and stderr. The managed-state normalizer now reads any non-code GitHub update_error as github_remote_lookup_failed, so upgraded workspaces never surface that text (for example in package doctor --detail deep). Stable codes and npm reasons are unchanged. A unit test covers the legacy text, a stable code and an npm reason.
